hints.title: Read the root information
hints.body: Compare x2−14x+9 with x2−(α+β)x+αβ. You need symmetric information about the roots, not their separate values.
hints.recap: For a monic quadratic, root sum is minus the linear coefficient and root product is the constant.
hints.pitfall: Taking square roots term by term does not preserve a sum.

recall.reminder: For a monic quadratic, root sum is minus the linear coefficient and root product is the constant.

hints.title: Square the new root sum
hints.body: The new product is αβ=αβ. For the new sum S=α+β, use S2=α+β+2αβ.
hints.recap: Squaring a sum introduces the cross term, linking root sum and product.

recall.reminder: Squaring a sum introduces the cross term, linking root sum and product.

hints.title: Choose the positive sum
hints.body: The new roots are positive, so their sum is positive. Use this sign when recovering the sum from its square. Then build a monic quadratic from your new root sum and product.
hints.recap: Build the new monic quadratic from its new sum and product.
hints.pitfall: The coefficient of x is the negative of the new root sum.
hints.pause: Calculate the two coefficients and check that they give the required sum and product.

recall.reminder: Build the new monic quadratic from its new sum and product.

solution:
Expanding the given factorisation shows α+β=14 and αβ=9. Since both roots are positive, αβ=3.

Let S=α+β. Then S2=α+β+2αβ=14+6=20. Also S>0, so S=20.

Therefore (x−α)(x−β)=x2−(α+β)x+αβ=x2−20x+3, option C. This avoids calculating the two original roots separately while retaining the required principal square-root signs.
knowledgePattern: Recover sum of square roots from Vieta's relations
